title: Inherent holiness never reaches the summit in this life
source_text: XXIII. Porro justitia & sanctitas illa, ad quam fideles per Spiritus Sancti gratiam renovantur, quandiu durat hujus vitae tempus, nunquam pervenit ad summum, sed per-petuo opus habet augeri & perfici. Adeoque illi ipsi qui progressus in ea quam maximos fecerunt, ad mortem usque agnoscere debent se nondum perfectos esse; & assidue in id incumbere, ut in Christi gratia magis ac magis proficiant, sanctificationem perficientes in timore Dei. Id exemplo suo docet ipse Paulus, quem sanctitate nullus Apostolorum su-perasse videtur. Jam enim morti proximus, profiteretur se nondum metam apprehen-disse, neque jam perfectum aut consummatum esse. Et postea subjungit, Unum autem ago, ea quidem quae a tergo sunt obliviscens, ad ea vero quae a fronte sunt contendens, scopum versus pergo ad palmam supernae vocationis Dei in Christo Jesu. Phil. 3. 14. Idcirco homines etiam sanctissimos spectat Angeli vox illa ultimo Apocalypseos, Qui justus est justificetur adhuc, & qui sanctus est sanctificetur adhuc.
pass_a_gloss: Further, that righteousness and holiness to which believers are renewed by the Holy Spirit's grace, so long as this life's time lasts, never reaches the summit, but continually needs to be increased and perfected. And therefore even those who have made the greatest progress in it ought to acknowledge until death that they are not yet perfect, and assiduously to set themselves to advance more and more in Christ's grace, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God. Paul himself teaches this by his own example, whom none of the apostles seems to have surpassed in holiness. For already near death he professes that he has not yet grasped the goal, nor is already perfect or consummated. And afterward he adds: But one thing I do: forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus (Philippians 3:14). Therefore that angelic voice at the end of the Apocalypse also regards even the most holy men: He who is righteous, let him be justified still; and he who is holy, let him be sanctified still.
pass_b_english: In this life inherent holiness never reaches the summit; it must always grow.
Paul near death had not attained; the Apocalypse still urges the just to be justified yet more.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1057.
